prompt:
You are a photoreal interior visualization assistant. The attached image is a screenshot of a simple 3D scene of a real flat under renovation: true room geometry with placeholder furniture blocks. Turn it into a photorealistic interior photograph of the same room from the same camera.

Preserve exactly, from the reference image: room shape and proportions; the position, count and size of every wall, window, door and opening; ceiling height 2.7 m; the camera position, angle, field of view and framing; and the zoning of the furniture — every large item stays where its block stands, with the same footprint and orientation. Keep the input aspect ratio; do not crop or re-frame.

Within each block you may replace the placeholder with real furniture of the same category, size and orientation, refine its silhouette to the style below, and add finishing materials, textiles, plants, light fixtures and small lived-in details. Kitchen unit composition, appliance models and mirror shapes may vary within the same footprint.

Style: warm modern minimalism (Organic Modern / warm Japandi) for a family of four with two young children and a dog. Clean architectural lines softened by rounded, organic furniture silhouettes — no sharp corners, no thin spindly legs.

Palette: warm white and light beige/greige walls and ceiling as the base; sage-green and forest-green accents (cabinetry, textiles); light and medium-dark natural wood tones (chestnut, pine) for furniture and decor. No cold greys, no bright saturated colors, black used only as a small accent (fixtures, hardware, faucets).

Materials: matte sage-green HPL kitchen fronts (no gloss) — base units, appliance column, fridge and the visible sides of the wall units — while the wall-unit doors are a warm beige matching the floor tile, with a faint wood grain and no colour variation; a plain white matte HPL worktop and backsplash of one tone; chrome or gunmetal plumbing fixtures; a wide rectangular kitchen sink with a combined main+filtered-water faucet; tile flooring in the hallway and kitchen zone; warm-toned quartz-vinyl (SPC) flooring in living rooms; natural woven jute/sisal rugs. Wood shows its grain under a matte lacquer; stone shows depth in its veining; upholstery reads as a woven weave, never as vinyl.

Furniture: rounded, low-profile, substantial silhouettes; sofa without armrests, deep seat, dense durable upholstery (bouclé or performance-weave fabric) in a warm neutral tone; round or soft-edged coffee tables in wood or stone.

Lighting: layered warm light (~2700K), no single central ceiling fixture — recessed spotlights, integrated LED strip lighting along cabinets, shelves and niches, a few small sconces as accents only. Light comes from the windows and from the fixtures already visible in the reference, falls off towards the far corners, and every object casts a contact shadow where it meets the floor. The view through a window keeps its detail instead of burning out to white.

Decor: minimal and natural — wood and bamboo accessories in chestnut/pine tones. The floor stays clear: every plant that appears must be a small one standing on a shelf, a windowsill or a worktop. This flat has no floor-standing plants and no plants in baskets or pots on the floor — that space belongs to the people and the dog. No frescoes, no figurines, no moldings or ornate trim, no visual clutter, no readable text or brand logos. A slightly lived-in, realistic level of tidiness is welcome, not a showroom-perfect scene.

Windows: minimal blackout roller blinds mounted tight inside the window recess — no fabric curtains or drapery of any kind.

Cabinet fronts: a wardrobe, a tall unit or a kitchen run keeps the width and the number of doors given with its dimensions — a 1.77 m wardrobe with 4 doors shows exactly four leaves of 44 cm, it does not stretch along the wall or split into six narrow ones. Handles stay flush or recessed, in the style below.

Mirrors: the reference marks every mirror, and a mirror stays a mirror — a frameless glass panel reflecting the room back, never turned into a door, a window, a picture or a wardrobe front. The tall mirror in the hall is 0.90 m wide and 2.40 m high on a plain wall; the bathroom mirrors sit above their basins. Their reflections show the room they stand in, lit as the room is lit.

Openings: a plain rectangle on a wall is a doorway or a mirror as the shot notes say, never an invented window. Windows and balcony doors exist only where the reference shows them.

Camera: an architectural lens matching the field of view stated with the dimensions below, natural depth of field, straight verticals, no fisheye or barrel distortion, sharp across the room.

## r10-street
Loggia 4.5 m² (1.19 × 3.78 m, ceiling 2.7 m), a cutaway view: the camera stands outside the building where the glazing wall normally is, looking west across the whole loggia at its back wall. The glazing has been removed from the reference on purpose — render the loggia as an open section, with no glass, frame or railing between the camera and the room, and no street or facade in the frame. The far wall is the wall to the kitchen with a doorway 1.60 m wide and 2.10 m high; through it the kitchen-living room is visible (green and beige kitchen fronts, dining table). On the left (south end) a hung oak desk 0.80 m deep across the full width with a wooden chair, and a deep IT shelf above it at 2.0 m with a LED strip under its front edge; on the right (north end) a floor-standing shelving unit 0.40 m deep, drawers below, open sections above. Sliding doors on this wall close the doorway from the loggia side: the reference shows their exact state (open or closed, which side the leaves park on, how far they stand proud of the jamb) — keep it, the leaves are plain flat panels in the wall colour with flush pulls. Painted greige walls, dark grey porcelain tile floor. Keep the ceiling light strip as it is.
Real dimensions of this shot, in metres — respect them, the room is small: floor 1.19 × 3.78 (4.5 m²), ceiling 2.70. The camera stands 1.55 m above the floor, tilted 2° down, with a 60° field of view — an eye-level photograph on a normal lens, no wide-angle stretching and no barrel distortion.
